title: Barcelona in advanced negotiations over five-year renewal for La Masia midfielder
tweet: Barcelona are in advanced talks to extend Brian Farinas’ contract by five years, raising his release clause from €20 m and keeping him as a registered first‑team No. 4. The deal, still pending, would lock him to the club beyond 2030 and halt the Girona move that nearly saw him leave. As things stand, the agreement looks closer than ever, but the final signature remains to be seen.

title: Barcelona captain eager to renew his contract and lead team to greater heights
tweet: Raphinha has netted eight goals in five games, proving his value as Flick’s first captain. As things stand, Barcelona aims to add one or two years to his 2028 deal, but formal talks are yet to begin. The real question is whether the club will match his rising market value.

title: Confirmed: Barcelona superstar named La Liga Player of the Month for August
tweet: Raphinha has been voted La Liga Player of the Month for August, a result that underlines his eight goals in five games and a 100 % start for Barcelona. As things stand, the award could strengthen his bid for a new contract, though the final decision remains to be seen.

title: Spain manager endorses Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal for Ballon d’Or: ‘I think he can win it’
tweet: Luis de la Fuente said Lamine Yamal can win the Ballon d’Or because he is Spanish and a great footballer; as things stand the endorsement boosts his profile but the award will still hinge on the 2026 season performance and the competition from Rodri and Harry Kane.

title: Barcelona among top clubs tracking Borussia Dortmund youth prodigy – report
tweet: Barcelona are now monitoring 15‑year‑old Justin Ejodamen from Dortmund’s U16 side; he’s already broken youth records and scored a viral halfway‑line goal. The club’s interest is limited by transfer rules until he turns 16, so the focus remains on tracking his progress.

title: Barcelona emerge as Europe’s most prolific attacking force in 2026/27
tweet: Barcelona’s first five competitive matches produced 22 goals – 4.4 a game – a scoring rate that leaves Bayern, Chelsea and even Real Madrid far behind, with Raphinha already eight and Yamal five.
